STATION: West Shore of Alburgh Point of the Tongue
BLOOMINTENSITY: 2 - Cyano present - less than bloom levels (include photos)
DETAILS: Kayaking from the iron railroad bridge in North Hero to Alburg dunes, I encountered numerous spots that had cyanobacteria starting to accumulate on the surface.  All were low level 2 or bad 1d, none were worse than that, but it was very widespread, in spots along my route in 1 square mile.   My route was from the point on the map north to the Alburg Dunes beach, west along the beach, then south in the middle of the lake.   It may have been a little worse on the east side of the lake, close to the tongue.  I did not see major accumulations near the shore but I rarely got close enough to see.  The beach at the park was pretty clear.  The attached photos are from spots along the tongue, roughly 100 yds offshore, along roughly 1 mile of my trip, ending at the east end of Alburg Dunes beach.   I'll submit another report regarding my trip back in the middle of the lake.  I assume you can get the location from the geo tags on the photos.  Let me know if you want more info on the locations.

BLOOMINTENSITY: 2 - Cyano present - less than bloom levels (include photos)

Unfortunately the lighting on the north shore made it difficult to observe or photograph with the shadows. Seems to be clearer by the shore but may still have some cyano among the veg. BLOOMINTENSITY: 2 - Cyano present - less than bloom levels (include photos)

Extent in corner 20x20ft and today has spread southward between the corridor of vegetation and rock shore for @100ft. Narrows to about 2ft wide at the south end (near the railroad bridge). The water is disturbed near the bridge from gentle wind and water flow under the bridge.  No accumulations noticed farther east of the bridge along the south shore of lake to the condos unit. Sharing several photos to document the bloom condition - shows different lighting can hind or expose the condition. The wide-A is what I can see overlooking the area; wide-AA different angle and enhanced the image; close view is what see looking down at close range (the same area that has the sun reflection in the wide-AA view).  North side is clearer near the shore and still turbid in the boat dock area, can not see what is within the veg.) No sample.

Cat 2 is most obvious near the southern bulkhead area where material does tend to get push. North side was so turbid could not see the bottom. I am not sure if there might have been some recent boat movement, also as approached watched a flock take flight which may also stirred up the area. Difficult to see if cyano was present.
